synthesis.description: The gas risk team keeps the price curves and location mappings used to value positions current. A round starts when a trader, a desk or a system change needs a curve added, a location remapped or a subregion code changed. Darron Giron, and later Kam Keiser, sets up the curve, asks the desk how it should be mapped, circulates the day's curve lists and official post IDs, and answers questions about curve moves. In the Netco transition, curve files were rebuilt, checked for retired curves and moved to a new directory before loading.
steps: A desk, trader or system change raises the need for a new curve, a remapping or a code change.
The risk analyst asks the desk how the location or deal set should be mapped.
The analyst sets up the curve following the written procedure and adds it to Tagg and the publication names.
The analyst records the official post ID and circulates the updated curve lists or mappings.
Desks check their regions for locations mapped to curves that will no longer be set and send back a list.
Questions about curve moves are answered with the traders' explanation of the market.
synthesis.approach: Keep one curve and location mapping register that a routine check compares with the official books: it flags locations mapped to retired curves, records the official post ID, and generates the circulated curve list, so the analyst only decides new mappings with the desk.
synthesis.rationale: The mail already shows a written procedure for setting up a curve and a macro that queries official books; a single SOP that joins set-up, mapping questions, post ID recording and list circulation would let any analyst run a round the same way, which mattered when the work moved from one person to another during Netco.
